terms.definition: Simple Storage Service — AWS's scalable, durable object storage service that stores data as objects inside buckets, accessible from anywhere via HTTP/HTTPS
terms.example: Like a limitless cloud hard drive where every file has a unique URL and can be accessed by anyone with the right permissions

terms.definition: A storage model where data is stored as discrete objects (data + key + metadata), accessed via APIs, not mounted as a disk or file system
terms.example: Contrast with EBS (block storage like a hard drive) and EFS (file storage like a network share)

terms.definition: A container for S3 objects — every object must be stored inside a bucket. Buckets have globally unique names and are created in a specific AWS region
terms.example: Like a folder on the internet — name must be unique worldwide, like a domain name

terms.definition: A unit of data stored in S3, consisting of the data itself (file content), a key (unique name), and metadata (properties like content-type and size)
terms.example: A file called 'invoice-2024.pdf' stored in a bucket, with key='billing/2024/invoice-2024.pdf' and metadata Content-Type=application/pdf

terms.definition: The unique name of an object within an S3 bucket — can include '/' characters that visually simulate directory paths, but S3 has no real directory structure
terms.example: 'users/john/profile.jpg' is the full key; the slashes appear as folders in the console but are just part of the name

terms.definition: S3 bucket names must be unique across ALL AWS accounts and regions worldwide — no two buckets anywhere on AWS can share the same name
terms.example: If bucket 'my-photos' already exists in any account anywhere, you cannot create another 'my-photos' — try 'john-my-photos-2024'

terms.definition: The default S3 storage class — replicates data across 3+ AZs, provides 99.999999999% durability and 99.99% availability, for frequently accessed data
terms.example: Best for active data: website files, application assets, real-time analytics

terms.definition: Infrequent Access storage class — multi-AZ, lower storage cost than Standard, but a per-GB retrieval fee applies. Minimum storage duration 30 days
terms.example: Compliance reports accessed once a month — storage savings outweigh the retrieval fee

terms.definition: Single-AZ infrequent access storage — lowest-cost IA option, but data may be lost if the AZ fails
terms.example: Backup of data that already exists elsewhere — dev environment snapshots, secondary copies

terms.definition: Automatically moves objects between access tiers based on usage patterns — no retrieval fees, small monthly monitoring fee per object
terms.example: When you don't know how often objects will be accessed — let AWS decide the optimal tier

terms.definition: Archive storage with millisecond retrieval — for data accessed quarterly (every 90 days). Minimum storage 90 days
terms.example: Medical images archived after 90 days but occasionally needed for patient revisits

terms.definition: Archive storage with 1-12 hour retrieval — for backups and archives where retrieval urgency is low. Minimum storage 90 days
terms.example: Monthly database backups kept for compliance — you can wait a few hours if you need to restore

terms.definition: The cheapest AWS storage class — retrieval takes 12-48 hours. Minimum 180-day storage. For data retained for years but almost never accessed
terms.example: 7-year financial records required by regulations — pay the lowest rate; accept slow retrieval

terms.definition: An S3 feature that splits large objects into parts, uploads them in parallel, then assembles them. Required for objects > 5 GB, recommended for > 100 MB
terms.example: Uploading a 50GB video file — split into 500 parts of 100MB each, upload simultaneously, finish 10x faster

terms.definition: A bucket feature that preserves all versions of every object, including deleted ones — enables recovery from accidental deletion or overwrites
terms.example: Enable versioning: upload v1 of config.json, then upload v2 — both versions are stored. Delete it — a delete marker hides it but both versions remain recoverable

terms.definition: A special object created by S3 when versioning is enabled and an object is deleted without specifying a version ID — hides the object but doesn't permanently remove versions
terms.example: Delete an object → delete marker created. Remove the delete marker → object reappears. Both operations are reversible

terms.definition: A JSON-based IAM resource policy attached to an S3 bucket that defines who can access it and what actions they can perform
terms.example: Allow all authenticated users to GetObject, or allow a specific EC2 role to PutObject — all defined in JSON on the bucket

terms.definition: Protection for S3 data: SSE-S3 (AWS-managed keys, default since 2023), SSE-KMS (customer KMS key), SSE-C (customer-provided key), or client-side encryption
terms.example: All new S3 objects are encrypted with SSE-S3 by default since January 2023 — no configuration needed

terms.definition: A bucket-level setting that blocks all public access to the bucket and its objects, regardless of bucket policies or ACLs — enabled by default on all new buckets
terms.example: New buckets have Block Public Access ON — you must explicitly turn it off to host a public website

terms.definition: A WORM (Write Once Read Many) feature that prevents objects from being deleted or overwritten for a retention period — even by root account. Governance or Compliance mode
terms.example: Store financial records with 7-year Compliance mode lock — not even administrators can delete them before the retention period expires
